content:
**Highest elevations (average/official city‑center altitude) of the five most‑populated cities in the world**  
*(city‑proper populations, latest estimates ≈ 2023‑2024)*  

| Rank (by population) | City (Country) | Approx. 2024 City‑Proper Population* | Official/average elevation (m above sea level) |
|-----------------------|----------------|--------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------------|
| 1 | **Tokyo** (Japan) | ~ 14 million (city proper) | **≈ 40 m** – The Tokyo metropolitan area sits on the Kantō plain; the city‑center (Shinjuku/Chiyoda) is listed at about 40 m (130 ft) above sea level. |
| 2 | **Delhi** (India) | ~ 11 million (city proper) | **≈ 216 m** – Delhi’s municipal elevation is recorded at 216 m (708 ft). The city spreads across the Indo‑Gangetic plain, with the central area around this height. |
| 3 | **Shanghai** (China) | ~ 24 million (city proper) | **≈ 4 m** – Shanghai is a low‑lying coastal city on the Yangtze River delta; the official elevation is about 4 m (13 ft) above sea level. |
| 4 | **São Paulo** (Brazil) | ~ 12 million (city proper) | **≈ 760 m** – The city sits on a high plateau; the municipal elevation is listed at 760 m (2 493 ft). |
| 5 | **Mexico City** (Mexico) | ~ 9 million (city proper) | **≈ 2 240 m** – Built in the Valley of Mexico, the capital’s average altitude is about 2 240 m (7 350 ft) above sea level. |

\*Population figures are rounded to the nearest million and reflect the most recent United Nations/World Bank city‑proper estimates (2023‑2024).  

### How the elevations were obtained
- **Tokyo:** Wikipedia “Tokyo” page lists “Elevation: 40 m (130 ft)”.  
- **Delhi:** Wikipedia “Delhi” page lists “Elevation: 216 m (708 ft)”.  
- **Shanghai:** Wikipedia “Shanghai” page lists “Elevation: 4 m (13 ft)”.  
- **São Paulo:** Wikipedia “São Paulo” page lists “Elevation: 760 m (2 493 ft)”.  
- **Mexico City:** Wikipedia “Mexico City” page lists “Elevation: 2 240 m (7 350 ft)”.

These elevations are the standard reference points used for each city (typically the elevation of the city hall or central administrative district) and represent the typical height at which the majority of the urban area sits.
